title: Parts of the interoceptive system lie outside the blood-brain barrier

statements.text: Interoceptive neurons in peripheral ganglia and in some central nuclei are exposed to molecules in the blood. Circumventricular organs such as the area postrema and subfornical organ lack the barrier and connect to central interoceptive regions such as the nucleus tractus solitarius.

sources.quote: interoceptive neurons in peripheral nerve ganglia as well as in nuclei of the central nervous system are at the mercy of molecules in the blood circulation
certain regions, known as circumventricular organs (CVOs), lack this barrier and allow free exchange between blood and neural tissue
